question: to the Commission Lídia Pereira (PPE), Sebastião Bugalho (PPE), Paulo Cunha (PPE), Paulo do Nascimento Cabral (PPE) Subject:

The Letta report1 (April 2024) proposed a fifth freedom of movement in the single market for research, innovation, data, skills and education – an idea already put forward by Jacques Delors in 1989. Two years on and we have yet to achieve this fundamental condition to reverse the slowdown in European competitiveness. Despite initiatives such as Choose Europe for Science and the European Health Data Space, there is still no integrated strategy for the free movement of researchers, knowledge and data. Given that the EU’s share of global patents has been falling and that 90 % of public investment in research and innovation remains national and focused on domestic priorities, this issue is becoming particularly pressing. Can the Commission therefore say: 1.
What legislative or non-legislative initiatives does it intend to pursue, and what the timeline would be, to formally enshrine the fifth freedom of movement in the single market?
Does it envisage setting up a European grant for deep tech, with rules tailored to risk finance?

Does it believe it is the right moment to set up a European Joint Knowledge Centre, in line with the Letta report, based around a centralised digital platform providing access to publicly funded research, data and educational resources?
https://www.consilium.europa.eu/media/ny3j24sm/much-more-than-a-market-report-by-enrico-letta.pdf
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (7.8.2026) As announced in the Competitiveness Compass1 and the One Europe, One Market Roadmap2, the Commission is preparing a legislative proposal for a European Research Area (ERA) Act, targeted for adoption in the second half of 2026. The ERA Act will contribute to implementing the Fifth Freedom by improving framework conditions for research and innovation, notably through measures supporting attractive research careers, mobility, knowledge circulation and open science. The Commission is also advancing these objectives through existing initiatives such as the ERA Policy Agenda3, the ERA Talent Platform4, the Union of Skills5 and Choose Europe for Science6. The European Innovation Council already provides a combination of grants and equity investments for breakthrough innovation and high-risk deep tech. The Commission proposes to reinforce these instruments under the next Multiannual Financial Framework and is also advancing the proposal for a Scaleup Europe Fund to help address financing gaps for strategic European companies. The European Open Science Cloud (EOSC)7 realises the vision of a European Knowledge Commons through the EOSC Federation8, a federated ‘system of systems’ enabling researchers to store, share, process, analyse and reuse Findable, Accessible, Interoperable and Reusable (FAIR) research outputs across Europe. Rather than establishing a new centralised structure, EOSC is expanding as an interoperable infrastructure, which addresses the fragmentation and under-exploitation of publicly funded research outputs. It also facilitates cross-border access and collaboration in an open, secure and trusted environment, while developing synergies with other European Common Data Spaces and strategic data initiatives.
